blocks.content: Organizational structure is the formal framework that defines how tasks are divided, grouped, and coordinated within an enterprise.

rows: Grouped based on functions or specialized skills (e.g., HR, Finance, Marketing)
Grouped based on distinct products, service lines, or geographical regions
Single, vertical hierarchy led by functional department heads
Semi-autonomous divisions operating with independent division managers
Centralized decision-making at the top management level
Economies of scale with low duplication of resources
Higher operational costs due to duplication of resources across divisions

items: Matrix structures violate Henri Fayol's principle of Unity of Command due to employees reporting to two managers simultaneously (Functional and Project Managers).
Distinguish clearly between Delegation (granting authority to a subordinate) and Decentralization (systematic dispersal of authority across all management levels).
V.A. Graicunas Theory calculates the mathematical relationships between a superior and subordinates based on span of control.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Organizational structure defines how activities such as task allocation, coordination, and supervision are directed toward achieving organizational goals.
Line organization is the oldest and simplest form of organizational structure, characterized by a direct vertical scalar chain of authority.
Matrix organizational structure combines functional and divisional structures, resulting in a dual chain of command.
Span of control refers to the number of subordinates a manager or supervisor can directly and effectively manage.
Decentralization delegates decision-making authority down to lower levels of hierarchy, promoting agility and local responsiveness.
